verdict.summary: Composio has no managed Pipedrive OAuth app, so you have to register your own. A private app skips review and can be shared with any Pipedrive company through an unlisted install link once you set it live. Review is only needed for a public app listed in the Marketplace, and that review takes up to 21 business days, sometimes longer.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for a private app; 1-2 days to prepare a Marketplace submission (listing assets, legal pages, demo video)
verdict.time_to_first_connection: 20-30 min (after you have a developer sandbox account)
verdict.approval_wait: None for a private app. Up to 21 business days for a Marketplace listing (one report of 28+ days)

gates.name: Draft app (private or public) in a developer sandbox
gates.unlocks: You can create the app, get a client_id and client_secret, and authorize users in the company where the app was created.
limits: You need a developer sandbox account before Developer Hub appears
A draft app can only be seen and installed by users in the company that created it
Only one callback URL per app
Access tokens last 60 minutes; a refresh token expires if unused for 60 days

gates.name: Private app in live status (unlisted install link)
gates.unlocks: Any Pipedrive company can install the app through a direct, unlisted installation link. There is no Marketplace listing and no review.
limits: The docs state no per-company or install cap, but treat that as unknown rather than confirmed
App type is set at creation and cannot be changed to public later

gates.name: Public app approved and published in the Pipedrive Marketplace
gates.unlocks: A public listing in the Pipedrive Marketplace that anyone can find and install.
limits: After approval the app stays unlisted until you click Publish
Changing the callback URL, scopes or app extensions after approval triggers another review
Existing users must reinstall to get newly added scopes
gates.time_to_reach: Up to 21 business days of review (one report of 28+ days), plus your prep time

steps.title: Get a Pipedrive developer sandbox account
steps.detail: Sign up for a Pipedrive developer sandbox account. Developer Hub, where apps are created, only appears for accounts that have one.
gotchas: Without a sandbox account you will not see Developer Hub in Settings.

steps.title: Open Developer Hub
steps.detail: In Pipedrive, open the Settings menu, click your company's name and pick Developer Hub. Click the green "Create an app" button (or "+ Create an app" if you already have apps).

steps.title: Choose private or public app type
steps.detail: Pick "Create private app" if only your own users and customers will install it through a direct link. This option has no review. Pick "Create public app" only if you want a Marketplace listing, which requires review.
gotchas: The app type cannot be changed later in Developer Hub. Choosing wrong means creating a new app.

steps.title: Set the callback URL
steps.detail: Fill in the app's basic info. In the callback URL field, paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio Pipedrive auth config. This field is the OAuth redirect_uri, and it must match the redirect_uri sent in the authorize request.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Only one callback URL is allowed per app, so you cannot register both a local dev URL and the Composio URL.
You can save a placeholder at first, but update it before the OAuth flow goes live.
On a public app, changing the callback URL after approval triggers another review.

steps.title: Select only the scopes you need
steps.detail: On the OAuth & access scopes tab, select only the scopes your agent actually calls; base is always on. Don't copy Composio's default list (contacts:full, leads:full, mail:full, activities:full, products:full, projects:full) unless you use every one. Use read variants wherever writes aren't needed.
gotchas: Users can only accept or deny all requested scopes together.
Marketplace review rejects apps that request scopes they don't use.
If you request admin, the app must still work when a non-admin installs it.

steps.title: Copy client credentials into Composio
steps.detail: Copy the client_id and client_secret from the OAuth & access scopes tab. In Composio, create a Pipedrive OAUTH2 auth config using these credentials and the same scope list you selected in Pipedrive.
gotchas: Composio has no managed Pipedrive app, so your own credentials are required for OAuth. The other option is API key mode.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a connection through Composio and authorize with a user in the company where the app was created. Confirm the token exchange works and that an API call succeeds with the granted scopes.
gotchas: The authorization code expires 5 minutes after it is issued.
Access tokens last 60 minutes. Refresh tokens expire after 60 days without use, and then the user must reinstall.

steps.title: Set the private app live and share the install link
steps.detail: For a private app, change its status from draft to live in Developer Hub. Share the direct, unlisted installation link with the companies that should connect. No review is required.
gotchas: In draft status, only users in your own company can install the app.

steps.title: Prepare Marketplace listing assets and legal pages
steps.detail:
Public apps only. Draft the following:
- A unique app name
- A summary of 150 characters or less
- A description of 1,500 characters or less
- A 1:1 icon, at least 256x256 px (PNG or JPG, up to 10 MB)
- At least 3 screenshots (maximum 5)
- A Terms of Service page and a Privacy Policy page
gotchas: The docs disagree on screenshots (checklist: 3-5; registration form: 1 required). Provide at least 3.

steps.title: Meet the technical review checklist
steps.detail:
Make sure the app does all of the following:
- Uses OAuth 2.0
- Refreshes tokens after their 60-minute lifetime
- Requests only the scopes it needs
- Has tested install and uninstall flows
- Never collects or stores a user's personal API token
- Respects rate limits and uses v2 webhooks where possible
- Handles different user types and permission sets

steps.title: Record demo video, sign agreement and submit
steps.detail: Record a demo video explaining how each scope is used. Set up working test accounts and give a reachable contact. Accept the Developer Partner Agreement, then submit the public app for review in Developer Hub.

steps.title: Wait for Pipedrive review
steps.detail: Review can take up to 21 business days, and one developer reported waiting 28+ days with no feedback. Pipedrive sends the result by email and shows it in Developer Hub. A rejection email lists the reasons, which must be fixed before you resubmit. Send questions to marketplace.devs@pipedrive.com.

steps.title: Publish the approved app
steps.detail: An approved app stays unlisted until you click Publish in Developer Hub. After publishing, changes to the callback URL, scopes or extensions go back through review. Listing images can be edited without review.
gotchas: Adding a scope later means existing users must reinstall to get it.

requirements.detail: Needed before Developer Hub is visible.

requirements.item: Single callback URL matching Composio's redirect
requirements.detail: One callback URL per app. It must match the redirect_uri in the authorize request.

requirements.item: Private app set to live status
requirements.detail: Lets other companies install through an unlisted link without review.

The app must use OAuth 2.0, refresh tokens every 60 minutes, request minimal scopes and have tested install and uninstall flows. It must not store users' API tokens, must respect rate limits, should use v2 webhooks where possible and must handle different user types and permissions.

requirements.item: Developer Partner Agreement, Terms of Service and Privacy Policy
requirements.detail: Required by the legal section of the approval checklist.
The demo video must explain how each scope is used, the test accounts must work, and the contact must be reachable.
You need a unique name, a summary of 150 characters or less, a description of 1,500 characters or less, a 1:1 icon of at least 256x256 px (PNG or JPG, up to 10 MB) and 3-5 screenshots.

scopes.effect: Always on. Gives read-only access to the current user and settings.
No separate review tier is documented. Review checks that every scope is necessary, so drop unused ones or use read variants. These are in Composio's default list.
Included in Composio's defaults. Drop it unless the agent really uses the mail endpoints, because unused scopes get apps rejected.
The installing user must be a company admin. The app must still work, or fall back gracefully, when a non-admin installs it.

blockers.symptom: Developer Hub doesn't appear in Settings
blockers.cause: Your account isn't a developer sandbox account.
blockers.fix: Create a developer sandbox account and open Developer Hub from there.

blockers.symptom: Marketplace review rejects the app over its scopes
blockers.cause: The app requests scopes it doesn't use, such as Composio's default mail:full or projects:full.
blockers.fix: Trim scopes to the endpoints you actually call, then explain each one in the demo video.

blockers.symptom: Redirect mismatch, or 401 'unauthorized access' from oauth.pipedrive.com
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri doesn't match the single registered callback URL, or the client_id is wrong.
blockers.fix: Paste the exact Composio callback URL into the callback URL field and check the client_id in Composio.

blockers.symptom: Other companies can't install the app
blockers.cause: The private app is still in draft status, which only allows installs from your own company.
blockers.fix: Set the private app to live and share the installation link.

blockers.symptom: Connections break after a period of inactivity
blockers.cause: Refresh tokens expire after 60 days without use.
blockers.fix: Refresh tokens regularly, or have the user reinstall.

blockers.symptom: 429 Too Many Requests until the next day
blockers.cause: The company's daily token-based API budget is used up. A separate per-token burst limit also applies on a rolling 2-second window.
blockers.fix: Reduce call volume and back off on 429 responses.

blockers.symptom: App shows the wrong type, or can't be moved to the Marketplace
blockers.cause: App type is fixed at creation.
blockers.fix: Create a new app with the correct type.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Pipedrive, so for OAuth you must register your own app in Developer Hub and paste its client_id and client_secret into a Composio OAUTH2 auth config. The other option is Composio's API key mode. Use the Composio callback URL as the app's single callback URL. Trim Composio's broad default scopes before any Marketplace submission. A private app in live status lets your users connect without review.

open_questions: The docs don't document any install cap, user cap or rate limit for unreviewed or unlisted (private live) apps. Treat this as unknown, not as confirmed absent.
It isn't clear whether a developer sandbox company can be used for real production data, or whether your production Pipedrive account must install the live private app through its link.
Whether a public app (as opposed to a private one) can be installed by other companies before approval isn't stated beyond 'needed to be listed'.
The docs don't say whether any scope triggers extra review or a security assessment.
PKCE support isn't documented. Confirm with Pipedrive before building a PKCE-only client.
The screenshot count conflict (3-5 in the checklist vs 1 required in the registration form) is unresolved.
The Developer Partner Agreement terms and any fees were not verified.
Pipedrive's acceptance of Composio's backend.composio.dev callback as the registered callback URL was not confirmed.
